All are welcome to join Bishop Alan McGuckian SJ as he celebrates this Mass in particular for those who have died in this past year. Children’s Liturgy 11am Mass Hello children! Today Jesus tells us about the kind of person who will be welcome in his kingdom. The gospel today reminds us that we are all God’s children and that Jesus is in each one of us. And so, every time we help someone else, every time we treat someone kindly, welcome them or share with them, then we are doing this to Jesus. This week, let’s all try to remember that Jesus is in every person and to treat people as Jesus wants us to. God of all, show us how to answer your call so we may see your kingdom a place where no one is hungry, thirsty, or alone here on earth. Amen. Today we celebrate the last Sunday of the Liturgical Year, known as the Solemnity of Our Lord Jesus Christ, King of the Universe . We began moving toward this goal with the First Sunday of Advent. Today we have reached it. Given the fact that the Liturgical Year represents our own life in miniature, this experience reminds us, and even more educates us, that we are on a journey toward an encounter with Jesus, the Spouse, when He will come as the King and Lord of life and of history. The coming we are now awaiting is His second coming. His first coming was in the humility of a Child laid in a manger. His second coming will be when He returns in glory at the end of time which we liturgically celebrate today. But there is also an intermediate coming – we are living it today – in which Jesus is present in us through the Grace we receive in the Sacraments and in the face of every “least one” the Gospel speaks of (“ Unless you turn and become like children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven” . Mt. 18:3). We are invited to recognize Jesus in the face of each brother and sister. Along this journey, the liturgy offers us a school of life to instruct us how to recognize the Lord present in everyday life and to prepare us for His final coming. PRAYER TO ST MICHAEL THE ARCHANGEL Holy Michael the Archangel, defend us in the hour of battle. Be thou our safeguard against the wickedness and snares of the Devil. May God restrain him, we humbly pray, and do thou, O Prince of the heavenly host, by the power of God, thrust down to Hell, Satan and with him all the evil spirits who wander through the world for the ruin of souls. Amen. The Solemnity of Our Lord Jesus Christ King of the Universe 22nd November 2026 Saintfield & Carrickmannon Parish Bulletin Fr Martin Graham PP
